summary: Ten of the twelve findings are confirmed and two are rejected. Confirmed: 1 (high: both Part II design jobs ignore the accepted extensions RS-32 and RS-17, a make_queue defect that also affects five other parents), 2, 4 (high: items 31 and 33 are routed into the finished AdicEtaleGeometry blueprint and are planned nowhere), 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12. Fixes are corrected for 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12; in particular finding 12's replacement note would introduce a new false library claim (Tau Ceti proves completeness of the module topology on finite modules, completeSpace_moduleTopology). findings.reason: Confirmed. In make_queue.paper_designs, lines 432–437, part-ii routes are grouped by parent and each job is named '<base>PartII'. The switch to Part III happens only when that literal id is in data/atlas.json. I ran accepted_routes and paper_designs read-only on the current tree. They produce DESIGN-AnalyticToricGeometryPartII and DESIGN-DeligneWeightsAndPurityPartII, each carrying only this paper's route ('1 continuation'). Both jobs are pending in queue.json, and issues #4583 and #4584 are open with the label state:available. RS-32 (REV-RS-32: 'accepted after corrections') keeps the id ShimuraCompactifications and retitles it 'Analytic toric geometry, Part II: arithmetic toroidal compactifications'. RS-17 (accepted) makes WeightsInEtaleCohomology 'Deligne weights, purity and the Weil bounds, Part II: …'. data/atlas.json still carries the old titles. The extraction, its review and the design brief never mention RS-32 or RS-17. The overlap is real: C0 keeps 'extension of affine toric charts to the required base rings', and C2 glues torus embeddings. Leaf (1) glues X_{Σ,A} over any A (compare RT-AREA-algebraicgeometry/34, confirmed). One nuance: a second sibling 'Part II' is not an error in itself. Accepted RS-06, RS-08 and RS-21 give Modular forms three of them. The harm is that the job does not know the existing extension, plus the overlap. Corrected fix: (1) Do not make ShimuraCompactifications or WeightsInEtaleCohomology the roadmap-level first prerequisite. ShimuraCompactifications requires ShimuraData, ShimuraVarieties, PELModuli and more, and R34.6 depends on 'each actual automorphic realization'. Either choice would put Shimura or eigenform theory upstream of Theorem 9.6. Keep each parent as the first prerequisite. In route 5's brief, name ShimuraCompactifications as the existing Part II. Import at stage level C0's charts, and the general-base X(Σ) once RT-AREA-algebraicgeometry/34 settles its owner. Plan only what C0 lacks. In route 6's brief, name WeightsInEtaleCohomology as the existing Part II and say that R34.6 may consume Theorem 9.6. Whether the new roadmap is called 'Part III' or stays a subtitled sibling Part II is the maintainer's choice. (2) In make_queue, read the accepted extensions (action extend) from data/restructure/*.result.json and put their ids and titles in the design brief. If the job switches to Part III, also replace the hard-coded '{base}PartII' in the 'built' sentence. A simulation shows that it would otherwise say 'AnalyticToricGeometryPartII is already in the atlas', an id that does not exist. (3) Regenerating the queue keeps old jobs (the extra_old merge). So the two DESIGN-…PartII jobs and their reviews must be marked superseded, and issues #4583 and #4584 closed or relabelled. Holding them until regeneration is not enough. Severity: High is defensible: both jobs can be claimed now, and the defect is systemic. The same miss affects five other parents, EllipticCurves, ModularForms, JacobianChallenge, ProfiniteCohomology and ArithmeticDirichletSeries. The switch works only where the RS extension literally has the id '<base>PartII' (ModularCurves, ReductiveGroups).

Item 23 is Huber's statement in the category of adic spaces: morphisms Y → Spa(R, R⁺) for sheafy (R, R⁺) (paper p. 258, Proposition 2.19). The promoted AdicEtaleGeometry blueprint does not own it. Node A1/maps-from-adic-spaces-to-yoneda-affinoids proves a bijection for morphisms X^Y → Spa^Y(A, A⁺) of J_rat-sheaves, by Yoneda and the sheaf property of O_X. Its sentence 'For (A, A⁺) sheafy and X^Y replaced by X, this is Huber 1994, Proposition 2.1(ii)' is an attribution, and no proof step establishes it. The same blueprint's request to tauceti AdicSpaces Layer 5 asks for exactly 'morphisms from an adic space T into Spa of a complete sheafy pair (R, R⁺) are the morphisms of pairs … (Huber 1994 Proposition 2.1(ii))'. Its neededBy lists A1/maps-from-adic-spaces-to-yoneda-affinoids itself and A1/adic-spaces-in-yoneda-adic-spaces, whose full-faithfulness step uses Hom_Adic(Spa(O_X(U)), X'). So A1 uses the statement and does not plan it. AdicSpacesPartII also requests it (request (b)) and imports it in R0/affinoid-fibre-product. The anchor's Layer 5 (content/tau-ceti/AdicSpaces/README.md, 5.1–5.4) does not list it. 'Missing' is therefore right, and the review's wording ('neither … states it') is accurate. PerfectoidSpace.spaHomEquiv is only in the unpromoted PerfectoidSpaces packet (review needs_changes). The live decomposition's P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting uses 'Huber's Prop. 2.19' as an input. I did not use PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15. Lead check: I read the promoted blueprint's A1/maps-from-adic-spaces-to-yoneda-affinoids statement and proof steps and its Layer-5 request (A), and the anchor's Layer 5 text (5.1–5.4); the verdict above holds. The finding's side remark is right, though: AdicSpacesPartII does use the statement, as an import. Since route 2 points into the AdicSpacesPartII blueprint, which was promoted on 28 September before this extraction merged, item 23 is also planned nowhere, as with finding 4. The fix job for finding 4 should add a Huber 2.1(ii) node to AdicSpacesPartII:R0, or record the owner question for the maintainer.

Mechanics: make_queue.py lines 912–914 put an accepted source route into ADDED_SOURCES. That dictionary is read only by added_sources() in add_blueprint (line 1018), as extra BP prompt text. The merge step copies 'state' from the existing queue, so a done BP job is never re-run. make_source_jobs.py only re-pins restricted-book citations. followups.py could re-queue an unfinished blueprint with the regenerated prompt, but the queue has no continuation (~N) blueprint jobs, so that path is unused. The extraction (#4556) and its review (#4572) merged on 2026-09-29. Route 4 therefore points into a finished, promoted blueprint, and items 31 and 33 are planned nowhere. No A1 node states Proposition 2.27 or 2.29 (p. 263). A1's stage text owns sites, geometric stalks and field pairs for them. The owner gap is real. AdicSpacesPartII asks anchor Layer 5 for 'the completed residue affinoid field κ(y) … with its canonical morphism Spa κ(y) → Y'. R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres, R0/fibre-over-point and R0/maximal-point-closure-rational cite Huber (1.1.8)–(1.1.10) in their proof steps, but no node states these results. Anchor Layer 1.5 develops specialisation 'only as needed' for Theorem 7.10. The paper uses both results: the proof of Corollary 6.7(iii) ('any x ∈ X factors as a composite R → k(x)^ → Γ ∪ {0}') and the proof of Proposition 7.16 (maximal generalisations). High severity stands. Corrected fix: As proposed, with these adjustments. R0/fibre-over-point uses κ(y), requested from the anchor, and does not build it. Make the two new AdicSpacesPartII:R0 nodes prerequisites of R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres, R0/fibre-over-point and R0/maximal-point-closure-rational, in place of their bare Huber (1.1.8)–(1.1.10) citations. In the extraction, drop route 4 and mark items 31 and 33 planned at AdicSpacesPartII:R0 once the amendment lands. A source route into the finished AdicSpacesPartII blueprint would be inert for the same reason. Keep the maintainer note.

The red team judged against the PerfectoidSpaces--P0 packet, which is not a live plan. Its review is 'needs_changes' ('the packet is not accepted'), and it is absent from data/blueprints and data/promotions.json. For P2 and P3 the live plan is the stage text plus the reviewed decomposition data/decompositions/PerfectoidSpaces.json. REVIEW-EXT-03 accepted it; the build merges it into the atlas and trims it only for layers that a promoted packet replaces. In that decomposition, node P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids states '(Prop. 7.7) In characteristic p an etale map of perfectoid spaces is locally the base change of an etale map U' → V' of affinoid noetherian adic spaces over K'. It adds 'Prop. 7.7 and Cor. 7.8 follow by the same reduction' and cites Propositions 7.6–7.7, so item 106 is planned at P3. Node P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields records that 'the ramification-theory proof imports GR Propositions 6.6.2, 6.6.6 (deeply ramified fields; …) and 6.3.6', and P3's coverage lists these as remaining P3 work. Item 37's note describes exactly this node. The summary's '90-odd items are planned by P0–P3, P5 and P7' refers explicitly to this decomposition. Two sub-claims are also inaccurate. 'Deeply ramified' does occur in packet text, in P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields. Remark 3.3 is not proved in the paper, which cites [15, Proposition 6.6.6]. One sentence is inaccurate: route 1's reason, as rewritten by the review, says the packet 'replaced the 33-node decomposition'. That is a low-severity wording error, not a status error. Lead check: data/decompositions/PerfectoidSpaces.json carries review status 'accepted' (REVIEW-EXT-03); the PerfectoidSpaces--P0 packet's review is 'needs_changes' and it is absent from data/promotions.json. If that packet is later accepted as it stands, items 37 and 106 lose their owner, so its next review must reconcile them. Route 1's reason, which says the packet 'replaced' the decomposition, is a low-severity wording error that the fix job for another finding may correct in passing.

The duplication holds against the live plan, not only against the packet node cited. The reviewed decomposition data/decompositions/PerfectoidSpaces.json has PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma: Lemma 6.5 for K⟨T_0^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ with f homogeneous of degree d ∈ ℤ[1/p], and Corollary 6.7(i). Its proof steps are the induction 'c → c' = c + a', ε(c), Lemma 6.4's O_X(U_c♯)°a and 'g_{c'} = g_c + Σ (ϖ♭)^{c+1−ε+ε(c')} (g_c/(ϖ♭)^c)^i s_i'. Leaf (5) of route 5 asks the toric Part II to write out the same induction, and item 133's note says it 'must write the induction out'. The cited node, P2/approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc, is in the unpromoted packet and generalises the base to a perfectoid Tate ring. The paper (p. 306) says: 'Now the analogue of Lemma 6.5 holds true for R, with the same proof.' §15 requires the lemma to be planned once, in P2, in the generality its uses need. The leaf (1) sub-claim is half right. Leaf (1) says the affine charts and Gordan finite generation are 'imported from … C0 … and not rebuilt', so nothing rebuilds Gordan. It does build fan gluing over any ring A, with no comparison to Tau Ceti AnalyticToricGeometry Layer 0 items 7–9 (affine toric schemes and fan gluing over ℂ), which §15's last bullet requires. DESIGN-AnalyticToricGeometryPartII is still pending, so the fix can still be applied. Corrected fix: Leaf (5): import the P2 approximation lemma, which today is PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma of the reviewed decomposition and becomes P2/approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc once the packet is promoted. Add a requests entry to PerfectoidSpaces:P2 for the same statement over Banach-completed perfected monoid algebras K⟨C ∩ (M × ℤ)[1/p]⟩ of a rational polyhedral cone C, graded by a ℤ[1/p]-valued linear functional. The polydisc is the positive orthant with total degree; R_D is the cone ⟨u, v_i⟩ ≥ −j a_i, graded by j. The toric Part II then keeps only the identification of R_D with such an algebra and of its tilt. Leaf (1): Gordan is already imported, so nothing needs removing. Require that X_{Σ,ℂ} agree with the fan scheme of Analytic toric geometry Layer 0 item 9, and take the dual semigroup and its finite generation from Layer 0 item 6.

R24.5/compatible-system-predicates says 'strictly pure if strictly compatible with each WD_v(ℛ) pure of weight w' but never defines purity of a WD representation. Confirmed at low severity. Page 309 reads: 'By Theorem 3.6(a) of [21], there is some open neighborhood Ỹ of Y^ad_K in X^ad_{Σ,K} such that Ỹ_{C_p} and Y^ad_{C_p} have the same Z/ℓZ-cohomology.' Reference [21] is Huber, 'A finiteness result for direct image sheaves on the étale site of rigid analytic varieties', J. Algebraic Geom. 7. This is a general result about étale cohomology of adic spaces. Route 6's brief says 'Prove or import Huber's theorem [Hub98, Theorem 3.6(a)]', and it names an owner only for Theorem 9.7 (H5). Item 146 is in route 6's item list, and its note says 'Routed to the weight-monodromy Part II'. So the owner can be worked out, and only the brief's wording is unclear; hence low. H5 is a plausible home: its text covers 'the cases of Hub96 Theorems 3.7.2 and 3.8.1 … used in ECD §27' and 'overconvergent-sheaf continuity statements'. Two supporting claims are overstated. First, BKV is not accepted work: its review verdict is 'revise', and its extraction never mentions Huber. Second, BKV (arXiv 2207.00369, §4) proves 'a motivic analogue of [Hub98a, Theorem 3.6]', and its Remark 4.3 says 'we need the smoothness assumption contrary to Huber's result'. So BKV does not use the ℓ-adic theorem. The only packet hit for 'Hub98' (HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas) is about compactly supported cohomology, a different Huber result. Corrected fix: H5 is not 'in review'. It belongs to the BP-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H4 job (scope H4 and H5), which is claimed externally, and the merged H0 packet covers only H0–H3. A source route to H5 would reach that blueprint as a new source and would widen H5 beyond its ECD §27 scope. Route 6 is the only consumer, so the simpler option is to keep item 146 in route 6. Its brief should then say 'Prove here Huber's theorem … with the hypotheses of Hub98a Theorem 3.6(a)'.
